properties.description:
FFWTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
North Central Pima County in southeastern Arizona...
Southwestern Pinal County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 130 AM MST.

* At 1055 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated a couple of rounds of
thunderstorms this evening had produced between 1.00 and 3.50
inches of heavy rain along and east of Route 15 between Santa Rosa
and North Komelik. The heaviest rainfall, between 2.50 and 3.50
inches, occurred near and east of North Komelik. Flash flooding is
ongoing, especially in normally dry washes and low-lying areas that
drain into the Santa Rosa Wash.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
North Komelik.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Anegam Wash, Sil Nakya Wash and Santa Rosa Wash.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued August 24 at 12:44AM CDT until August 24 at 9:00PM CDT by NWS Fort Worth TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with temperatures and heat index
values up to 111 expected.

* WHERE...North and Central Texas.

* WHEN...Until 9 PM CDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat and high humidity events.
properties.instruction:
Take extra precautions when outside by staying hydrated, wearing
lightweight and loose fitting clothing, and limiting strenuous
activities to the early morning or evening. Check up on relatives and
neighbors. Never leave young children or pets in an enclosed vehicle,
even for a short time, as temperatures can quickly rise to
life-threatening levels.

Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke. To
reduce risk when outdoors, the occupational safety and health
administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in shaded
or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat should be
moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an emergency!
Call 911 ASAP if you or someone you know is exhibiting signs of heat
stroke.

Extreme heat is dangerous, especially for those without reliable
shelter. Limit time outdoors during the hottest time of the day,
typically from 2 to 7 PM, rest in the shade when possible, and drink
plenty of water. Locate nearby cooling centers through local
resources or dial 2-1-1 in Texas.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following river and
location in Indiana...

less chance of rain Wednesday afternoon and night.

* WHERE...White River at Hazleton.

* WHEN...Until late Friday evening.

flood. Flood gates must be installed at Hazleton.

- There is no current observed data.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 19.6
feet Wednesday morning. It will then fall below flood stage
late Friday morning.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
The National Weather Service in Medford has issued a Red Flag
Warning, which is in effect from 11 AM to 8 PM PDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.

* AFFECTED AREA...In California, Fire Weather Zones 280 and 281.
In Oregon...Fire Weather Zones 621, 622, and 623. In California,
this includes Scott Valley, Shasta Valley, and the Klamath River
Valley. In Oregon, this includes the Siskiyou Mountains, the
Southern Cascade Mountains, and the Rogue Valley.

* WIND...In Oregon, west to northwest winds 10 to 15 mph with
gusts around 25 mph. In California, south to southwest winds 10
to 20 mph with gusts around 30 mph.

* HUMIDITY...Daytime humidities down to 8 to 15 percent.

* DETAILED URL...View the hazard area in detail at
https://weather.gov/wrh/hazards?wfo=mfr
properties.instruction:
Follow all fire restrictions. You can find your county's
emergency sign up form as well as links to fire restrictions at
weather.gov/medford/wildfire. One less spark, one less wildfire.

Be sure you're signed up for your county's emergency alert
system. Familiarize yourself with your emergency plan and make
sure you listen to emergency services. Visit ready.gov/plan for
more information.

A Red Flag Warning is issued when we identify weather conditions
that promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-
threatening. This does not mean there is a fire. These conditions
are either occurring now or will begin soon. It is important to
have multiple ways to receive information from authorities.

Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat

properties.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to
lessen the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

officials for more details.
